newsitem.title: USA: US House Democrats sharply criticize Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US House Democrats sharply criticize Greenspan.

text.p: Democratic lawmakers sharply criticized Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday for holding back economic growth and not doing enough to help the country's poor.
The barrage of comments came at the start of a House Banking subcommittee hearing on the economy.

"The Federal Reserve system under your governance ... has become an engine for inequality in our society," Rep. Barney Frank from Massachusetts told the central bank chief. "That has terribly negative consequences."
"The Federal Reserve seems to have forgotten there are communities in America that are in a persistent cycle of poverty and stagnation," New York Rep. Floyd Flake added.

Another New York lawmaker, Rep. Maurice Hinchey, criticized the Fed for restraining growth and voiced fears that the central bank was poised to raise short-term interest rates at its next policy-making meeting on March 25.
"We are fearful that would have consequences that would reduce economic strength," he added.
Perhaps the harshest criticism of Greenspan came from independent Bernard Sanders from Vermont.
Sanders attacked the Fed chief for calling for changes in the way the government calculates cost of living increases for pensioners on Social Security and others who receive government benefits.

"Maybe you'll tell this committee the last time you sat in a room with low income senior citizens and asked them how they're ging to survive if they lose $100 a year in their social security benefits," the independent lawmaker said.
Greenspan has argued that the consumer price index (CPI), which is now used to calculate cost of living increases for government benefits, significantly overstates inflation.
